Subject: Acme bake-off: discovery recap & next steps (benchmarks + acceptance criteria)

Hi Jane / Mark —

Thanks again for taking the time today — really helpful conversation. Quick recap while it's fresh and to make sure we’re aligned on next steps for the bake-off.

Pain points and goals
- Production latency spikes and token cost variability during peak search/card generation flows.
- Current solution struggles with long-context state (20k tokens) when re-ranking and multi-turn system prompts.
- Primary goal: consistent p50/p95 latency under target and predictable unit cost so engineering can set SLO-aligned budgets.

Current stack (what you told us)
- Inference: in-house TGI endpoints on GC instances for LLM serving; some experiments with vLLM on a single node.
- Orchestration: Kubernetes + custom autoscaler; simple kv-cache layer.
- Logging/metrics: Cloud monitoring + homegrown cost attribution.

Success criteria for bake-off (from your side)
- p95 latency at target load: <= 350ms for short prompts (<= 1k tokens), <= 900ms for long-context re-ranks (~10–15k active context).
- Cost target: reduce $/generated-token by >= 25% vs current TGI setup at production loads.
- Feature parity: support for streaming, function/tool calling, and KV/prefix caching.
- Determinism/quality: top-3 rank agreement with current system on hallmark eval set >= 90%.

Requested benchmarks we agreed on
1) End-to-end throughput + latency at 10k and 50k concurrent request/day profiles (p50/p95/p99).
2) Long-context re-rank benchmark using your 12k-context dataset (we'll accept sample subset with redacted PII).
3) Tokenization and cost delta report across quantization profiles we propose.
4) Comparison runs: vLLM (your current experiment), TGI on GC (your baseline), Redwood Dedicated pipeline (our recommended config).

Next steps & owners
- Marissa (me): I’ll share the bake-off runbook and a first-pass benchmark sheet (attached). I’ll also coordinate scheduling with the infra team for any dedicated window you need.
- Jane / Mark: please share the canonical eval set (or a representative redacted subset) and confirm required dates for the evaluation window.
- Ben / Dev (cc): can you review the benchmark sheet and confirm the run configs we should execute on Redwood Dedicated vs our vLLM/TGI comparators?

Attachments: acme_bakeoff_benchmarks.xlsx (spreadsheet with requested workloads), acceptance_criteria.md (proposed pass/fail), redwood_bakeoff_runbook.pdf (execution/runbook).

If that aligns, I'll schedule a short sync next week to lock the run window and access.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Thanks for the thorough recap — this is great and matches our notes. A few clarifications:

- For the long-context re-rank, we need p95 <= 900ms at 5 QPS sustained per replica (we'll provide the QPS profile in the eval set).
- For quality, the 90% agreement is measured against our in-house ranker on the top-3 results using the 1k-sample holdout we’ll provide.
- We can share a redacted subset of the eval set by EOD Thursday (we’ll remove any PII). You can use that for the initial runs.

We're targeting the bake-off window of Sep 14–18 (inclusive) for the primary runs. Can you confirm Redwood availability for those dates and whether Dedicated nodes will require any onboarding lead time?

Also: Ben / Dev — we expect a short onboarding call for infra (30m) to set up network access and any load generation details. When are you available next week?

Thanks,
